title: What is the gap angle, and does seventy degrees fit?
description: Six angles are placed round a point O and a gap is left. All the angles round a point, with the gap, add up to three hundred and sixty degrees, so the gap is fifty degrees and a seventy degree angle does not fit. Keeko's doubt, that the gap looks wide enough, is tested and struck out.
teaching_notes: One idea: the angles round a point, including the gap, add up to a full angle. Watch for students who judge the size of the gap by eye.

source: Angles of 40, 60, 50, 30, 40 and 90 degrees are placed round a point O, leaving a gap AOI.
video_script.why: The child knows a full turn is three hundred and sixty degrees but has not yet used it to find a missing angle.
video_script.substitution: The known angles and the gap angle together fill the full angle round O, so the gap is what is left of three hundred and sixty.
video_script.anchor: Angles of 40, 60, 50, 30, 40 and 90 degrees are placed round a point O, leaving a gap AOI: find the gap angle, and say whether a 70 degree angle fits.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says seventy degrees will fit because the gap looks wide. The numbers show the gap is only 50 degrees, and 70 is more than 50.
video_script.payoff_line: The gap is fifty degrees, so the seventy degree angle does not fit

final_answer.value: The gap is 50°, so the 70° angle does not fit
final_answer.spoken: the gap is fifty degrees, so the seventy degree angle does not fit

never_show: the gap value before step three
maths_rules: All the angles round a point add up to 360 degrees.
70 is more than 50, so the 70 degree angle would overlap its neighbours and does not fit.
video_script.design: One idea: the angles and the gap fill the full angle, so the gap is what is left. Keeko's doubt is that the gap looks wide enough for seventy degrees.
